concerns.text: Task T009 restricts the primary CI path to 'TinyLlama-1.1B' exclusively. This silently weakens FR-001 which mandates generation across 'two open-source LLM checkpoints'. The task does not document this as a scoped exception or reference a scope-limitation amendment, effectively dropping a mandatory requirement.

Task T011 implements a 'Technical' control corpus using 'tech_reports' dataset. The spec (FR-001/US-1) and plan define the generation scope strictly around four phenomenological strategies. There is no requirement for a technical control set; this task introduces unapproved scope (semantic drift) without a corresponding spec amendment.

Task T012 implements 'runner_local.py' for 'phi-2' (2.7B). The spec (FR-001) and plan only authorize 'Mistral-7B' and 'Llama-7B' as secondary checkpoints. Introducing 'phi-2' is an unapproved model substitution that violates the 'Model Access' assumption and the specific checkpoint requirements of FR-001.

Task T034 implements a 'Turing-Style Operational Test'. The spec (FR-001-012) and Success Criteria (SC-001-003) focus exclusively on internal metrics (NLI, stability, markers) and human qualitative ratings. This task adds a complex, unrequested feature (indistinguishability test) that is not anchored to any FR or SC, representing unapproved scope creep.

Tasks T039a and T039b split FR-009 ('cite... OR perform sensitivity analysis') into two mandatory tasks. This violates the logical structure of the requirement (OR condition) by forcing the implementation of both, effectively weakening the requirement's flexibility and inflating the workload without spec approval.

Task T013 requires generating 'data/raw/generation_log.json'. This artifact is not defined in the spec's Success Criteria, the plan's data model, or the contracts. It is an orphan artifact introduced by the task without traceability to a requirement, violating the 'Single Source of Truth' principle.
